facts.text: Todt Hill rises 401 feet, the highest natural point in New York City and the tallest spot on the Atlantic coastal plain from Florida to Cape Cod.
The name Todt comes from the German word for death, a nod to the long‑used Moravian Cemetery that sits at the hill’s southwestern foot.
While the summit is cloaked in woodlands that belong to the Staten Island Greenbelt, the surrounding neighborhoods are some of the most exclusive residential areas on the island.
Early 20th‑century architect Ernest Flagg left his mark on Todt Hill with distinctive houses, a fieldstone water tower, and a Palm House that once housed greenhouses.
Founded in 1740, the Moravian Cemetery at Todt Hill’s base is Staten Island’s oldest active burial ground and one of the city’s most historic cemeteries.
Abraham Lakeman built the Lakeman‑Courtelyou‑Taylor House on Todt Hill in the late 1600s, and the home was designated a New York City Landmark in 2016.
